steps.name: QC and PCA diagnostics of batch/condition confound
caveats: Do not attempt any batch-correction transform (ComBat, limma removeBatchEffect, SVA) here — with a 6/6 perfect confound there is no residual batch-only variance to estimate; any correction would remove the condition signal itself
If DESeq2 is unavailable, fall back to edgeR TMM normalization or a simple CPM+log2 normalization, and note which was used
steps.question: How much of the transcriptome-wide variance in the 12000x12 count matrix aligns with the batch B1/B2 axis versus the treated/control axis, and are they in fact fully collinear as the metadata claims?
acceptance_criteria: Raw counts are loaded (12000 genes x 12 samples) and cross-checked against metadata.csv for sample identity, condition, and batch
Library size and count distribution QC (e.g. total counts per sample, gene detection rate) reported per sample
Counts are normalized (e.g. DESeq2 median-of-ratios or edgeR TMM, whichever library is available) and log-transformed for PCA
PCA plot colored by both condition and batch is produced, confirming whether PC1 (or the top variance-explaining PC) separates B1/B2 identically to control/treated
A cross-tabulation of condition x batch is output explicitly confirming the 6/6 perfect confound (all controls in B1, all treated in B2, no split cells)
Output states in plain text that condition and batch are structurally unidentifiable from each other in this design

steps.name: Treated vs control differential expression (batch unmodelable)
caveats: State prominently in the output that because batch B1/B2 is perfectly confounded with control/treated (6 controls all in B1, 6 treated all in B2), any gene called 'differentially expressed' may reflect a processing-batch artifact (reagent lot, run date, extraction batch) rather than a true treatment effect — this cannot be distinguished with the current design

Do not apply any batch-effect removal method before or after the DE test; state instead that resolving this requires a re-designed experiment with condition and batch not perfectly collinear (e.g. samples of each condition split across both batches)

Do not report the DE gene list as a validated treatment signature; report it as the output of the only statistical test the data supports, with the confound stated as a primary limitation of the result, not a footnote
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated (batch B2) and 6 control (batch B1) samples using raw integer counts?
acceptance_criteria: Differential expression is run with a standard count-based model (DESeq2 Wald test or edgeR/limma-voom) with condition as the sole model term — a batch term cannot be added because it is aliased with condition (design matrix would be rank-deficient)
Output table includes gene symbol, log2 fold change, raw p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (FDR) for all 12000 genes

Significant gene count reported at FDR < 0.05 and at FDR < 0.1, alongside a note that this list is the treated-vs-control (equivalently batch B2-vs-B1) contrast and the two cannot be statistically separated
MA plot and volcano plot are produced for visual QC of the DE call
Result file explicitly labeled to reflect that the effect estimated is condition-and/or-batch, not condition alone

steps.name: Functional enrichment of the DE gene list (confound-flagged)
caveats: This step must not be used to argue the DE signal is biologically genuine — enrichment of plausible-sounding pathways is not evidence against a batch artifact
Confirm gene-set resource availability and organism match before running; do not substitute mouse gene sets for this human lung dataset
steps.question: What biological pathways or gene sets are enriched among the genes differing between treated (B2) and control (B1) samples, understanding that this signal is inseparable from a batch effect?
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g. GO biological process, and hallmark/KEGG pathways if gene sets are available for Homo sapiens in the environment) is run on the significant gene list from T1S2 (FDR<0.05), using the full 12000-gene list as background
Top enriched terms reported with adjusted p-values

Output explicitly states that any enriched pathway could equally reflect a batch/technical artifact (e.g. stress-response, RNA degradation, or processing-related pathways commonly seen in batch effects) rather than the biological effect of treatment, given the confound identified in T1S1/T1S2
If no organism-appropriate (Homo sapiens) gene sets are found provisioned in the environment, step reports that gap explicitly rather than substituting a different organism's gene sets

plan.title: Treated vs control DE with confounded batch caveat
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context states plainly that batch (B1 vs B2) is perfectly confounded with condition (control vs treated) — every control sample is in B1 and every treated sample is in B2. This is a structural limitation, not a statistical nuisance: no computational method (ComBat, SVA, RUV, or a batch term in a linear model) can separate a batch effect from a condition effect when the two design variables are collinear across all 12 samples. Any 'batch-corrected' result would be a modeling artifact, because the correction step and the biological contrast would be estimating the exact same contrast in the design matrix. Leek et al. 2010 (Nat Rev Genet, PMID 20838408) is the classic reference on this exact failure mode: batch effects correlated with the outcome of interest lead to incorrect conclusions, and no adjustment recovers the confound. Given this, the only honest path is: (1) run the standard treated-vs-control differential expression exactly as the design specifies, since it is the only test the design supports, (2) explicitly quantify and report how much of the transcriptome-wide variance aligns with the batch/condition axis via PCA and clustering, so the magnitude of the confound is visible in the deliverable, (3) run functional enrichment on whatever DE list emerges, but flag every output as uninterpretable as a pure treatment effect. No batch-correction step is planned, because attempting one here would launder a design flaw into a false sense of correction rather than fixing it. The plan does not claim to resolve the confound — it cannot be resolved from this dataset — it delivers the requested DE analysis alongside the diagnostics needed to see the confound's footprint, and states the limitation as a hard caveat rather than a fine-print caveat.
